comments.body:
For architecture you have to be creative, most architecture students are not so talented in math/physics. The better students like to draw or make things with their hands.

I didn't study at ETH, but I think it is not that different from where I once studied. Expect a lot of hours working on projects and harsh criticism (which will feel more personal, because you have to put something of yourself in the design).

Then after 6 years you will realize that a lot you learned is not really applicable in the real world (working with clients/budgets/high demands). And they don't teach you anything about what is really important, the business side of it all.
comments.author: Competitive-Dot-3333
